body.purpose: The default: rows, facts, running text, menus, buttons.

small.purpose: Meta lines, column headers, strips, captions.

mono.purpose: Ids, paths, shas, commands, file names — never a costume.

title.purpose: A section heading inside a page, a card's project.

heading.purpose: A report's title, the kit's page title.

shadows.name: shadow-edge
shadows.purpose: The edge mark: a row changed in the last minutes; in the sidebar, a mini row whose run changed since the operator last opened it (its «новое»); inset, so marking a row moves nothing, and never a signal hue.

shadows.name: shadow-target
shadows.purpose: The target mark: the object a link opened, on the muted ground; the current item of a list off a card or a mini row. A list's scroller holds an item's whole box, so the mark draws all four sides.

shadows.name: shadow-open-row
shadows.value: inset 0 1px 0 0 var(--frame), inset 1px 0 0 0 var(--frame), inset -1px 0 0 0 var(--frame)
shadows.purpose: The open row's frame (OPEN_FRAME.row): an open row draws its top and sides in 1 px of its host's --frame — muted ink (OPEN_FRAME.muted), or ink on a link's target (OPEN_FRAME.target) — on the table and on ExpandingFindings.

shadows.name: shadow-open-detail
shadows.value: inset 0 -1px 0 0 var(--frame), inset 1px 0 0 0 var(--frame), inset -1px 0 0 0 var(--frame)
shadows.purpose: The open row's frame (OPEN_FRAME.detail): its detail draws its sides and bottom, so row and detail read as one block. The muted ground alone is about 1.1:1 on the dark paper; the frame clears 3:1 on both.

shadows.name: shadow-overflow
shadows.purpose: The overflow cue (OverflowCue): a hairline of muted ink at a box's bottom edge while its rows or an open detail run past it (scrollHeight > clientHeight), hidden at the scroll's end; drawn over the box, never a border or padding.

shadows.name: shadow-overflow-end
shadows.purpose: The overflow cue at a box's end: a markdown table in running text that runs past its box's right edge, hidden once the box is scrolled to its end.

motion.name: overlay
motion.purpose: Dialogs, menus and tooltips open and close in the library's primitive; nothing else animates, and reduced motion stops the fold's chevron.

breakpoints.name: shell
breakpoints.purpose: The shell's one viewport breakpoint: below it the sidebar becomes a band above the page, its run list a fixed 128 px of one-line 32 px rows whose scroll snaps to a row's top.

breakpoints.name: strip-full
breakpoints.purpose: The held-order strip writes its nouns from this host width up.

breakpoints.name: view-columns
breakpoints.purpose: A view's second column: «Журнал»'s 14 rem stage rail beside its list, a finding article's decision and verdict beside its text.

narrative.overview: A desk where one operator reads what his unattended runs did: a warm-grey sheet, ink for words, and nothing else asking for attention unless it waits on him. The world is the prototype's (tga/.claude/fsloop/prototype-viewer/template.html), kept and written down: its twelve colours, its system faces, its 13 px text at 1.45, its 8 px radius. fsloopUI adds no brand and no new direction. Two jobs shape it. Scanning — many runs, hundreds of findings — wants density: one line per row, tabular numerals, fixed widths so nothing jitters. Reading — a finding's rule, a report, a goal of 8 617 characters — wants measure: running text keeps its paragraphs, lists and code at a 75-character line. Light and dark are equal surfaces and follow the system.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-grey surface; colour only for signal (red, amber, green), shown as a 7 px dot beside a plain word.
13 px body at 1.45, 12 px mono for identifiers, tabular numerals for every count.
Flat: depth is a hairline or a 1 px ring; the one shadow is the toast's.
Nothing moves on its own: every late part has its box reserved, a live list holds its order.
Russian interface; what fsloop or a critic wrote is shown as written.

rules.name: The Signal-Only Rule
rules.body: A hue is a state the operator should act on (red, amber) or a thing done (green); work in progress — writing, verifying, landing — is neutral, because the run carries it and nothing is asked (rules/ui → Conventions 2). Severity is the one category with a tone: critical red, major amber, minor neutral.

rules.name: The Dot Rule
rules.body: A state's colour is a dot, never a fill, a badge, a border or coloured text (ui → Status color is a dot).

rules.name: The Contrast Floor
rules.body: Text tokens hold 4.5:1 on every ground they sit on (paper, muted, popover, code) in both themes; a signal tone, used only as a dot, holds 3:1 — fsloopui/src/ui/tokens.test.ts computes both from the token values.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that changes or aligns — a count, a tab's count, a time, a duration — is set in tabular numerals, and a count that changes keeps a box three digits wide (min-w-count).

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Running text stops at 75 characters (max-w-measure); a table or a code block inside it scrolls sideways in its own bordered box instead of widening the column.

rules.name: The Reserved-Box Rule
rules.body: Anything that appears after first paint has its box before it appears: a frame thumbnail (118 × 74), a count (three digits), the held-order strip's line (28 px), a loading state the size of the region it fills, scrollbar-gutter: stable on a scrolling region (rules/ui → Strict 1).

dos: Do take a state's word and tone from its shared map, through StatusDot.
Do reserve every late part's box: a count's three digits, a strip's line, a thumbnail's 118 × 74.
Do show «Загрузка…» with a spinner, centred, in a region already at its final size.
Do keep running text at its measure, and let a table inside it scroll sideways.
Do set ids, paths and commands in mono, and what a critic wrote as written.
donts: Don't use a skeleton, anywhere; the library's skeleton is never imported.
Don't colour a state as a badge, a fill, a border or a word; never a pulse on «работает».
Don't write a raw colour, radius or size in a component; the theme's token is the answer.
Don't bold the active tab or anything that toggles: a weight change shifts its neighbours.
Don't put content in a tooltip, an object in a side panel, or an event the operator did not start in a toast.
